overview: The two defining parameters of Michaelis-Menten enzyme kinetics, each describing a different aspect of an enzyme's behavior.
genZNote: Km is how clingy the enzyme is. Vmax is its top speed.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The substrate concentration at which reaction velocity is half of Vmax — an inverse measure of enzyme-substrate affinity.
aspects.valueB: The maximum reaction velocity achieved when the enzyme is fully saturated with substrate.

aspects.label: What It Measures
aspects.valueA: Enzyme affinity for substrate — a low Km means high affinity (saturates at low substrate).
aspects.valueB: Catalytic capacity/turnover — determined mainly by enzyme concentration and kcat.

aspects.label: Units
aspects.valueA: Concentration units (e.g. mM, µM), same as substrate concentration.
aspects.valueB: Rate units (e.g. µmol/min), same as reaction velocity.

aspects.label: Dependence on Enzyme Concentration
aspects.valueA: Independent of enzyme concentration — an intrinsic property of the enzyme-substrate pair.
aspects.valueB: Directly proportional to enzyme concentration — doubling enzyme doubles Vmax.

aspects.label: Graphical Representation
aspects.valueA: The x-axis value where velocity = Vmax/2 on a Michaelis-Menten plot.
aspects.valueB: The plateau/asymptote of the Michaelis-Menten curve.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Reflects substrate affinity; independent of enzyme amount.
aspects.valueB: Reflects maximum rate; scales with enzyme amount.
